          England vs Greece Prediction: Women's World Cup Play-Off Second Leg Preview
        
      
                          
                      Oct 12, 2026
          
                      Maya Shah / Author, Emily Millen / Design
                  
      
              
                      
                  
          

    
              
      
              
                    
Following a slightly unconvincing 3-1 victory on Friday, England will look to seal their place in Round 2 of the qualification play-offs for the 2027 Women's World Cup. We preview the second leg with our England vs Greece prediction.
England take a two-goal advantage into Tuesday's second leg against Greece after a 3-1 victory in Crete put them firmly in control of their FIFA Women's World Cup 2027 play-off tie.

The Lionesses extended their unbeaten run against first-time European opposition in competitive matches to 16 games (W14 D2) with Friday's win. Yet, against a side sitting 54 places below them in the FIFA rankings, it was far from the straightforward evening many had anticipated.

Greece arrived in the tie full of confidence after topping Group C4, winning three and drawing one of their four qualifying matches. Although they ultimately fell to their first defeat of the campaign, they demonstrated exactly why England had been warned against complacency.

For Sarina Wiegman's side, however, the result continued an impressive record in World Cup qualifying. England have now won 20 of their last 21 such matches (L1), scoring 110 goals and conceding just three times across those 20 victories.

Should England complete the job at the King Power Stadium, they will progress to a Round 2 play-off against either Slovakia or Ukraine. The latter hold a commanding 3-1 advantage after the first leg of their tie.
Against Greece on Friday, England's breakthrough came from Georgia Stanway, whose goal just before half-time once again underlined her importance to this side.

The Arsenal midfielder is now England's joint-leading scorer under Wiegman with 32 goals, level with Beth Mead, while her 34 senior international goals place her outright seventh in the Lionesses' all-time scoring charts.
Indeed, she is one contribution away from becoming the second player to reach 50+ goal involvements (also 17 assists) under the Dutch manager after Mead (58).
Her partnership with Keira Walsh remains central to England's success.

The Lionesses have won 40 of the 60 matches the pair have started together (D9 L11), while Walsh could make yet more history after starting each of England's last 24 matches in all competitions. This century, only Rachel Unitt (35), Steph Houghton (26) and Alex Scott (25) have enjoyed longer consecutive starting streaks.

Interestingly, Lucy Bronze’s absence means she has now missed back-to-back competitive England fixtures for the first time since Wiegman's opening six matches in charge between September and November 2021.
History suggests England should have little trouble seeing the tie through on home soil.

The Lionesses have won each of their last seven home matches against fellow UEFA nations by an aggregate score of 19-0 and have lost just one of their last 48 competitive home fixtures (W41 D6), a 2-1 defeat to France in May 2024.
Wiegman's side are also unbeaten across 26 home qualifiers (W24 D2), scoring 120 goals while remarkably keeping a clean sheet in every one of those matches.
The first leg brought some individual milestones.

Erica Meg Parkinson (18 years, 174 days) came off the bench to become England's youngest debutant since Lianne Sanderson in 2006, while Manchester United captain Maya Le Tissier netted her first senior international goal on her 15th appearance. England remain unbeaten in matches in which a United player has scored, winning 29 and drawing one of those 30 games.

Alessia Russo continued her impressive England form, as she both scored and assisted in a competitive match for England for the third time. The Arsenal forward has now registered 11 goal involvements in 11 World Cup qualifying appearances (nine goals, two assists).

Russo's strike in the 67th minute was her 23rd goal in 50 international starts. Among England players this century, only Mead (30) has scored more goals in her first 50 starts, while Kelly Smith also managed 23.

For Greece, Veatriki Sarri will return to familiar surroundings at the King Power. The midfielder has made four WSL appearances at the venue for three different clubs, winning just once, while one of her nine WSL goals came against England goalkeeper Hannah Hampton when Birmingham City faced Aston Villa in May 2022.
